pr_body:
Since signals are functions, they inherit some properties like `length` and `name`. These can lead to issues in user code where somebody may write `someArraySignal.length` instead of `someArraySignal().length`.

These changes aim to mitigate the issue by overriding these properties to be `unknown`.

Fixes #59394.
pr_comments:
There's an extended diagnostic to surface those mistakes in templates:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/b22677d761fd7af38ac27c7162837cdd9b93a750/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/extended/checks/interpolated_signal_not_invoked/index.ts#L107-L114
@JoostK interesting that it didn't fire for #59394. That being said, similar issues can come up in TS as well and it's pretty low effort to support on our end.

comments: This `signal.length` case is tricky since each function (including a signal getter) has a valid [`length` property](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/length)

@kav-viasat we've discussed it during the team's issue triage meeting and recognize that we don't detect (in a diagnostic) the case you are bumping into. We are going to keep this issue open to see how common / widespread the issue is and might add some checks if it is common enough.

Not taking action on it immediately since every additional check has cost (development, maintenance, checks perf overhead etc.).
